passage: When economist Timur Saidov interviewed owners of small bakeries about food-delivery apps, most turned out to be ______. They acknowledged that the apps could bring in customers from across the city, yet they worried that high fees would eat their profits and that they would lose touch with their regular customers.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The owners see both a benefit (new customers) and drawbacks (fees, losing touch with regulars). Choice B, “ambivalent” (having mixed feelings), fits.

Choice A is wrong because it captures only the positive half of their views. Choice C is wrong because the owners clearly understand how the apps work and what they cost. Choice D is wrong because “indignant” means angry at unfair treatment, which is too strong and ignores the benefits they acknowledge.
explanation_uz:
Egalar ham foydani (yangi mijozlar), ham kamchiliklarni (to‘lovlar, doimiy mijozlardan uzoqlashish) ko‘radi. B javob — “ambivalent” (ikkilangan, aralash his-tuyg‘uli) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: faqat ijobiy tomonni aks ettiradi. C noto‘g‘ri: egalar ilovalar qanday ishlashi va qanchaga tushishini yaxshi biladi. D noto‘g‘ri: “indignant” adolatsizlikdan g‘azablanishni bildiradi — bu juda kuchli va ular tan olgan foydani inobatga olmaydi.

passage: The rules of the coppersmiths' guild in the nineteenth-century town of Qorabuloq, as reconstructed by historian Otabek Nazirov from surviving records, were remarkably ______. They specified not only the price of every item a member could sell but also the thickness of the metal, the hours apprentices could work, and even the pattern stamped on each finished pot.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The rules controlled many small details, from prices to the pattern on each pot. Choice D, “exacting” (strict and demanding precision), fits.

Choice A is wrong because “lenient” (permissive) is the opposite of rules that control so much. Choice B is wrong because rules that specify thicknesses and patterns are precise, not vague. Choice C is wrong because the rules date from the nineteenth century and nothing concerns their age.
explanation_uz:
Qoidalar narxlardan tortib har bir qozondagi naqshgacha ko‘plab mayda tafsilotlarni belgilagan. D javob — “exacting” (qat’iy, aniqlik talab qiladigan) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: “lenient” (yumshoq, erkin) shuncha narsani nazorat qiladigan qoidalarning teskarisi. B noto‘g‘ri: qalinlik va naqshni belgilaydigan qoidalar aniq, mavhum emas. C noto‘g‘ri: qoidalar XIX asrga oid, ularning yangiligi haqida gap yo‘q.

passage: Entomologist Bahrom Yusupov noticed that the honeybees in his study hives were ______ on cold mornings, crawling slowly across the frames and barely flying at all. Once the sun had warmed the hives, however, the same bees became busy and quick.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The bees crawled slowly and barely flew on cold mornings, in contrast to being “busy and quick” later. Choice C, “sluggish” (slow and inactive), fits.

Choice A is wrong because nothing suggests the bees attacked. Choice B is wrong because the text is about how the bees moved, not how many there were. Choice D is wrong because the bees' color does not change with temperature in the text.
explanation_uz:
Sovuq ertalablarda asalarilar sekin o‘rmalagan va deyarli uchmagan; keyinroq esa “g‘ayratli va tez” bo‘lgan. C javob — “sluggish” (sust, imillagan) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: asalarilar hujum qilgani aytilmagan. B noto‘g‘ri: matn asalarilar soni haqida emas, qanday harakatlangani haqida. D noto‘g‘ri: matnda asalarilarning rangi o‘zgarmaydi.

passage: Most plants respond to drought by closing the tiny pores on their leaves, which reduces water loss. Botanist Sherzod Nazarov found that a desert shrub he studies does the reverse, opening its pores wider on the hottest days. This seemingly ______ strategy turns out to make sense: the evaporating water cools the leaves enough to keep them from being damaged by heat.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The shrub does “the reverse” of what most plants do, and “seemingly” plus “turns out to make sense” show the strategy first appears illogical. Choice D, “counterintuitive” (contrary to what one would expect), fits.

Choice A is wrong because opening pores wider during drought is risky, not cautious. Choice B is wrong because the text says the strategy only seems odd at first; calling it “seemingly efficient” would undercut the point that it really works. Choice C is wrong because the shrub's behavior is the opposite of what most plants do.
explanation_uz:
Buta ko‘pchilik o‘simliklarning “teskarisini” qiladi, “seemingly” (go‘yo) va “turns out to make sense” (aslida mantiqli ekan) iboralari strategiya dastlab mantiqsiz ko‘rinishini bildiradi. D javob — “counterintuitive” (kutilganiga zid) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: qurg‘oqchilikda teshiklarni kengroq ochish ehtiyotkorlik emas, tavakkal. B noto‘g‘ri: matnga ko‘ra strategiya avval g‘alati ko‘rinadi; “go‘yo samarali” deyish uning haqiqatan ishlashi haqidagi fikrni buzadi. C noto‘g‘ri: butaning xatti-harakati ko‘pchilik o‘simliklarnikiga teskari.

passage: Most exhibits at the Samarqand Road Museum focus on a single century or a single craft. Its newest exhibit is far more ______: it brings together pottery, textiles, coins, and manuscripts from twelve centuries and three continents.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The new exhibit is contrasted with exhibits that cover one century or one craft, and it includes many kinds of objects from twelve centuries and three continents. Choice C, “wide-ranging” (covering many different things), fits.

Choice A is wrong because it describes the older exhibits, not the new one. Choice B is wrong because the text says nothing about how long the exhibit will run. Choice D is wrong because nothing suggests the exhibit is incomplete.
explanation_uz:
Yangi ko‘rgazma bitta asr yoki bitta hunarga bag‘ishlangan ko‘rgazmalarga qarama-qarshi qo‘yilgan va unda o‘n ikki asr hamda uch qit’adan ko‘p turdagi buyumlar bor. C javob — “wide-ranging” (keng qamrovli) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: bu eski ko‘rgazmalarga xos, yangisiga emas. B noto‘g‘ri: ko‘rgazma qancha davom etishi aytilmagan. D noto‘g‘ri: ko‘rgazma tugallanmagani haqida hech narsa yo‘q.

passage:
The following text is from a short story.

Dilnoza's grandmother never wasted anything. She saved string in a tin box, reused every envelope that came to the house, and patched the same wool coat for twenty winters. The neighbors teased her for being so ______, but when hard times came, it was her pantry that fed half the street.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The grandmother “never wasted anything” and saved string, envelopes, and an old coat. Choice D, “thrifty” (careful with money and resources), describes this habit.

Choice A is wrong because it is the opposite of someone who saves everything. Choice B is wrong because, although she later feeds her neighbors, the neighbors tease her for her saving habits, not for giving things away. Choice C is wrong because nothing in her slow, careful habits suggests impatience.
explanation_uz:
Buvisi “hech narsani isrof qilmagan”: ip, konvert va eski paltoni saqlagan. D javob — “thrifty” (tejamkor) aynan shu odatni ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: hamma narsani saqlaydigan odamning teskarisi. B noto‘g‘ri: keyinroq u qo‘shnilarini boqqan bo‘lsa ham, qo‘shnilar uning saxiyligi uchun emas, tejamkorligi uchun hazillashgan. C noto‘g‘ri: uning sekin, puxta odatlarida sabrsizlik ko‘rinmaydi.

passage: When a new bridge opened across the river at the town of Qumariq in 1931, the ferry that had carried passengers between the two banks for sixty years quickly became ______. Within a year almost no one rode it, and its owners sold the boat for scrap.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
After the bridge opened, “almost no one rode” the ferry and it was sold for scrap, so the ferry was no longer needed. Choice B, “obsolete” (out of use because something newer replaced it), fits.

Choice A is wrong because it reverses the situation: people stopped using the ferry. Choice C is wrong because the text gives no information about ticket prices. Choice D is wrong because the ferry was abandoned because of the bridge, not because it was unsafe.
explanation_uz:
Ko‘prik ochilgach, paromga “deyarli hech kim chiqmay” qo‘ygan va u temir-tersak sifatida sotilgan. Demak, parom endi keraksiz bo‘lib qolgan. B javob — “obsolete” (yangisi paydo bo‘lgani uchun eskirgan, ishlatilmay qolgan) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: vaziyatni teskari qiladi — odamlar paromdan foydalanishni to‘xtatgan. C noto‘g‘ri: chipta narxi haqida ma’lumot yo‘q. D noto‘g‘ri: parom xavfli bo‘lgani uchun emas, ko‘prik tufayli tashlab qo‘yilgan.

passage:
The following text is from a short story.

Old Karim, who had repaired watches in the same narrow shop for forty years, was famously ______. Customers who expected friendly conversation went away disappointed: he would take a watch, study it in silence through his eyepiece, and state a price in as few words as possible. Yet no one in the bazaar doubted his skill, and the line outside his door never shrank.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
Karim works “in silence” and uses “as few words as possible.” Choice B, “taciturn” (saying very little), fits.

Choice A is wrong because it is the opposite of his behavior. Choice C is wrong because customers trust him and keep lining up. Choice D is wrong because “no one … doubted his skill.”
explanation_uz:
Karim “jim” ishlaydi va “imkon qadar kam so‘z” ishlatadi. B javob — “taciturn” (kamgap) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: uning xatti-harakatining teskarisi. C noto‘g‘ri: mijozlar unga ishonadi va navbatda turaveradi. D noto‘g‘ri: “hech kim uning mahoratiga shubha qilmagan”.

passage: Agronomist Feruza Tosheva had hoped that mixing crushed eggshells into garden soil would ______ the growth of tomato plants. After two seasons of trials, however, plants in treated and untreated soil grew to the same height and produced the same number of fruit.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
Tosheva “hoped” for an effect, and “however” introduces the disappointing result that the eggshells made no difference. So she had hoped they would improve growth. Choice D, “boost” (increase), fits.

Choice A is wrong because eggshells cannot record anything, and recording growth is not something one hopes soil will do. Choices B and C are wrong because a researcher would not hope to stop or slow her plants' growth, and the “however” would make no sense if she had.
explanation_uz:
Tosheva qandaydir natijaga “umid qilgan”, “however” esa tuxum po‘chog‘i hech qanday farq qilmagani haqidagi umidsiz natijani kiritadi. Demak, u o‘sishni yaxshilashni kutgan. D javob — “boost” (kuchaytirmoq, oshirmoq) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: tuxum po‘chog‘i hech narsani qayd eta olmaydi. B va C noto‘g‘ri: tadqiqotchi o‘z o‘simliklarining o‘sishi to‘xtashini yoki sekinlashishini kutmaydi; aks holda “however” mantiqsiz bo‘lardi.

passage: Over many generations, fish that colonize pitch-dark caves often lose their eyes. Biologist Shahnoza Mirzayeva argues that this loss is not simply a matter of eyes falling into disuse. Eye tissue requires a great deal of energy to maintain, and food in caves is scarce. For an animal that will never encounter light, then, eyes are worse than ______; they are a drain on resources that could be spent on growth or reproduction.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The structure “worse than ___; they are a drain” means the blank must name a milder problem: eyes in darkness are at the least unnecessary, and in fact they also waste energy. Choice D, “superfluous” (unnecessary), fits.

Choice A is wrong because “indispensable” (absolutely necessary) contradicts the idea that eyes are useless in total darkness, and “worse than indispensable” makes no sense. Choice B is wrong because “rudimentary” (undeveloped) describes the eyes' structure, but the sentence is about whether eyes are useful to an animal that never sees light. Choice C is wrong because “ornamental” implies a decorative purpose, which the text never suggests.
explanation_uz:
“Worse than ___; they are a drain” tuzilmasi bo‘sh joyda yengilroq muammo bo‘lishini talab qiladi: zulmatda ko‘z hech bo‘lmaganda keraksiz, aslida esa energiyani ham isrof qiladi. D javob — “superfluous” (ortiqcha, keraksiz) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: “indispensable” (mutlaqo zarur) ko‘z zulmatda foydasiz degan fikrga zid, “zarurdan ham yomonroq” esa mantiqsiz. B noto‘g‘ri: “rudimentary” (rivojlanmagan) ko‘zning tuzilishini tasvirlaydi, gap esa yorug‘likni ko‘rmaydigan hayvon uchun ko‘zning foydasi haqida. C noto‘g‘ri: “ornamental” bezak vazifasini bildiradi, matnda bunday ishora yo‘q.

passage: Critics have often described the paintings of Hamida Yorqulova as spontaneous, as if each canvas were finished in a single burst of inspiration. Her notebooks, recently donated to a museum, complicate that picture. For nearly every painting they contain dozens of preliminary sketches, along with notes on color mixtures and revisions dated months apart. Yorqulova's process, in other words, was ______.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The notebooks show dozens of sketches, careful notes on colors, and revisions made over months, which contradicts the critics' view. Choice B, “meticulous” (extremely careful and precise), fits.

Choice A is wrong because “extemporaneous” (done without preparation) restates the critics' view that the notebooks “complicate.” Choice C is wrong because “desultory” (lacking a plan, jumping from one thing to another) conflicts with the careful, sustained work the notebooks record. Choice D is wrong because “capricious” (changing on impulse) wrongly suggests her revisions were whims rather than planned steps.
explanation_uz:
Daftarlarda o‘nlab eskizlar, ranglar haqida puxta qaydlar va oylar davomida qilingan tuzatishlar bor, bu tanqidchilar fikriga zid. B javob — “meticulous” (o‘ta puxta, sinchkov) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: “extemporaneous” (tayyorgarliksiz) daftarlar shubha ostiga qo‘ygan tanqidchilar fikrini takrorlaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: “desultory” (rejasiz, tartibsiz) daftarlarda qayd etilgan puxta va uzoq mehnatga zid. D noto‘g‘ri: “capricious” (injiq, to‘satdan o‘zgaruvchan) uning tuzatishlarini rejali qadamlar emas, injiqlik deb noto‘g‘ri ko‘rsatadi.

passage: In laboratory tests, food chemist Dilshod Rahimov found that coating freshly cut apple slices with a thin film made from citrus peel could arrest the browning that normally begins within minutes of cutting. Coated slices still looked fresh after six hours, while uncoated slices had turned brown within half an hour.
stem: As used in the text, what does the word “arrest” most nearly mean?
explanation_en:
Coated slices stayed fresh for six hours while uncoated ones browned, so the coating stops the browning process. Choice C, “halt” (stop), fits.

Choices A and B are wrong because they reflect the police sense of “arrest” (holding or seizing a person), which does not apply to a chemical process. Choice D is wrong because the coating prevents browning; it does not draw it in.
explanation_uz:
Qoplangan bo‘laklar olti soat yangi qolgan, qoplanmaganlari esa qo‘ng‘irlashgan, demak qoplama qo‘ng‘irlashish jarayonini to‘xtatadi. C javob — “halt” (to‘xtatmoq) to‘g‘ri.

A va B noto‘g‘ri: ular “arrest” so‘zining politsiyaga oid ma’nosini (odamni ushlab turish, qo‘lga olish) aks ettiradi, kimyoviy jarayonga mos kelmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: qoplama qo‘ng‘irlashishni oldini oladi, uni o‘ziga tortmaydi.

passage: Residents of a new housing development on the edge of the city rarely complain in public about the noise from a nearby highway. When sociologist Bekzod Sattorov asked them to rank their neighborhood's drawbacks anonymously, however, noise topped nearly every list. Their public silence, Sattorov argues, reflects not contentment but ______: most residents told him they believed complaints would change nothing.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The silence is “not contentment,” and residents believe complaining “would change nothing.” Choice D, “resignation” (accepting something unpleasant because one feels it cannot be changed), fits.

Choice A is wrong because “complacency” (self-satisfied ease) is a form of the contentment the text rules out. Choice B is wrong because “indignation” (open anger at unfairness) does not explain why residents stay silent. Choice C is wrong because “ambivalence” (mixed feelings) does not fit residents who clearly rank noise as the worst drawback.
explanation_uz:
Jimlik “mamnunlik emas”, aholi esa shikoyat “hech narsani o‘zgartirmaydi” deb hisoblaydi. D javob — “resignation” (o‘zgartirib bo‘lmaydi deb, yoqimsiz narsaga ko‘nikish) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: “complacency” (o‘zidan mamnun xotirjamlik) matn rad etgan mamnunlikning bir ko‘rinishi. B noto‘g‘ri: “indignation” (ochiq g‘azab) aholining nega jim turishini tushuntirmaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: “ambivalence” (ikkilangan his) shovqinni eng katta kamchilik deb aniq belgilagan aholiga mos emas.

passage:
The following text is from a short story.

Mrs. Rahimova had spent the whole afternoon rehearsing what she would say to her landlord: a firm, dignified speech about the broken heater and the three letters he had ignored. But when he opened his door with a warm greeting and asked kindly after her son, her resolve ______. Within a minute she heard herself thanking him for his time and promising not to trouble him again.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
Mrs. Rahimova had planned a firm speech, but after the landlord's kindness she ends up thanking him and promising not to bother him, so her determination faded away. Choice C, “dissipated” (gradually disappeared), fits.

Choice A is wrong because “coalesced” (came together into a whole) suggests her resolve became stronger and more unified. Choice B is wrong because “burgeoned” (grew rapidly) reverses what happens. Choice D is wrong because “ossified” (hardened, became rigid) would mean she stuck firmly to her plan, which she does not.
explanation_uz:
Rahimova xonim qat’iy nutq tayyorlagan edi, ammo uy egasining iliqligidan so‘ng unga rahmat aytib, boshqa bezovta qilmaslikka va’da beradi — ya’ni qat’iyati yo‘qolib ketgan. C javob — “dissipated” (tarqalib, yo‘qolib ketdi) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: “coalesced” (bir butunga birlashdi) qat’iyati kuchayganini anglatadi. B noto‘g‘ri: “burgeoned” (tez o‘sdi) sodir bo‘lgan narsani teskari qiladi. D noto‘g‘ri: “ossified” (qotib qoldi) u rejasida qat’iy turganini bildirardi, lekin bunday bo‘lmagan.

passage: A comet's tail is a ______ feature. It forms only as the comet travels close to the Sun, when heat drives gas and dust off the comet's icy surface, and it fades away again as the comet moves back toward the cold outer solar system.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The tail forms near the Sun and fades away again, so it exists only for part of the comet's journey. Choice B, “transient” (lasting only a short time), fits.

Choice A is wrong because it reverses the meaning: the tail appears and disappears. Choice C is wrong because the text says nothing about the tail's size or mass. Choice D is wrong because, although comet dust can reflect light, the text focuses on when the tail exists, not how it looks.
explanation_uz:
Dum Quyoshga yaqinlashganda paydo bo‘ladi va yana yo‘qolib ketadi, ya’ni u kometa yo‘lining faqat bir qismida mavjud. B javob — “transient” (o‘tkinchi, vaqtinchalik) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: ma’noni teskari qiladi — dum paydo bo‘lib, yo‘qoladi. C noto‘g‘ri: dumning hajmi yoki massasi haqida gap yo‘q. D noto‘g‘ri: kometa changi yorug‘likni qaytarishi mumkin bo‘lsa ham, matn dumning qachon mavjudligi haqida, ko‘rinishi haqida emas.

passage: Psychologist Gulnora Hasanova found that employees who received brief, ______ praise such as “nice job” were no more motivated afterward than employees who received no praise at all. Only feedback that described exactly what a person had done well led to greater effort on later tasks.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The praise is contrasted with feedback that “described exactly” what was done well, and the example “nice job” could apply to anything. Choice C, “generic” (general, not specific), fits.

Choice A is wrong because “lavish” means abundant or extravagant, which conflicts with “brief.” Choice B is wrong because the text contrasts vague and specific praise, not honest and dishonest praise. Choice D is wrong because the timing of the praise is never discussed.
explanation_uz:
Bu maqtov nima yaxshi bajarilganini “aniq tasvirlagan” fikr-mulohazaga qarama-qarshi qo‘yilgan, “nice job” (yaxshi ish) misoli esa har qanday holatga mos keladi. C javob — “generic” (umumiy, aniq bo‘lmagan) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: “lavish” (mo‘l-ko‘l, haddan tashqari) “brief” (qisqa) so‘ziga zid. B noto‘g‘ri: matn samimiy va nosamimiy maqtovni emas, umumiy va aniq maqtovni taqqoslaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: maqtovning vaqti muhokama qilinmaydi.

passage: Many people picture spider silk as delicate, the kind of thread that breaks at the lightest touch. But when materials scientist Javlon Ergashev tested silk from the orb-weaving spiders he studies, he found the threads surprisingly ______: they could stretch to nearly twice their length without snapping.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
“But” signals a contrast with the idea that silk is delicate, and the colon explains that the threads stretch a lot without snapping. Choice B, “resilient” (able to withstand strain without breaking), fits.

Choice A is wrong because “brittle” (easily broken) repeats the mistaken view the text contrasts with. Choice C is wrong because the tests measured stretching, not stickiness. Choice D is wrong because how easy the threads are to see is not discussed.
explanation_uz:
“But” bog‘lovchisi ipak nozik degan fikrga qarama-qarshilikni bildiradi, ikki nuqtadan keyin esa iplar uzilmasdan ancha cho‘zilishi tushuntiriladi. B javob — “resilient” (zo‘riqishga chidamli, uzilmaydigan) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: “brittle” (mo‘rt) matn rad etayotgan noto‘g‘ri fikrni takrorlaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: sinovlar yopishqoqlikni emas, cho‘zilishni o‘lchagan. D noto‘g‘ri: iplarning ko‘zga ko‘rinishi muhokama qilinmaydi.

passage: Historian Malika Ortiqova argues that the letters of nineteenth-century merchant Said Akbarov have been ______ by earlier scholars. Those scholars quoted a handful of colorful passages about his adventures on the road but ignored hundreds of pages recording prices, debts, and shipping routes, material that could reveal how regional trade actually worked.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
Earlier scholars used only a few passages and ignored most of the letters, even though that material could be valuable. Choice C, “underutilized” (not used as fully as possible), fits.

Choice A is wrong because no one is said to have credited the letters to the wrong author. Choice B is wrong because the complaint is that the letters were not used enough, not that they were praised too much. Choice D is wrong because the letters still exist; the hundreds of ignored pages are described as available.
explanation_uz:
Avvalgi olimlar faqat bir nechta parchadan foydalangan va xatlarning asosiy qismini e’tiborsiz qoldirgan, holbuki bu material qimmatli bo‘lishi mumkin. C javob — “underutilized” (yetarlicha foydalanilmagan) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: xatlar boshqa muallifga nisbat berilgani aytilmagan. B noto‘g‘ri: muammo xatlar ortiqcha maqtalganida emas, kam ishlatilganida. D noto‘g‘ri: xatlar saqlanib qolgan; e’tiborsiz qolgan yuzlab sahifalar mavjud.

passage: Most bird species in the cloud forest studied by ornithologist Akbar Tursunov spend their entire lives within a few hundred meters of the tree where they hatched. Against that background, the ______ habits of the forest's violet-crowned hummingbirds stand out. Tagged individuals have been recorded more than forty kilometers from their nests, sometimes crossing two mountain ridges in a single day.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The hummingbirds “stand out” against birds that stay in one small area, and the last sentence shows them traveling long distances. Choice A, “peripatetic” (traveling from place to place), fits.

Choice B is wrong because “sedentary” (staying in one place) describes the other birds, not the hummingbirds. Choice C is wrong because “gregarious” (sociable, living in groups) is about company, not distance. Choice D is wrong because “crepuscular” (active at dawn and dusk) concerns timing, and the text gives no information about when the birds are active.
explanation_uz:
Kolibrilar bir kichik hududda qoladigan qushlar fonida “ajralib turadi”, oxirgi gap esa ular uzoq masofalarga uchishini ko‘rsatadi. A javob — “peripatetic” (joydan joyga ko‘chib yuruvchi) to‘g‘ri.

B noto‘g‘ri: “sedentary” (bir joyda qoluvchi) kolibrilarni emas, boshqa qushlarni tasvirlaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: “gregarious” (to‘da bo‘lib yashovchi) masofa emas, jamoa haqida. D noto‘g‘ri: “crepuscular” (tong va shomda faol) vaqtga oid, matnda qushlar qachon faolligi aytilmagan.

passage: The mountain cat that ecologist Kamola Rashidova studies is so ______ that, in three years of fieldwork, she has seen one with her own eyes only twice. Nearly everything she knows about the animal comes from motion-triggered cameras hidden along rocky trails.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
Rashidova has seen the cat only twice in three years and must rely on hidden cameras, so the animal is very hard to find or see. Choice A, “elusive” (hard to find or catch), fits.

Choice B is wrong because nothing suggests the cat attacks or threatens anyone. Choice C is wrong because an animal that is almost never seen is not common. Choice D is wrong because the text is about seeing the cat, not hearing it, and a noisy animal would be easier to find.
explanation_uz:
Rashidova uch yil davomida mushukni faqat ikki marta ko‘rgan va yashirin kameralarga tayanishga majbur. Demak, bu hayvonni topish yoki ko‘rish juda qiyin. A javob — “elusive” (qo‘lga tushmaydigan, ko‘zga kam ko‘rinadigan) to‘g‘ri.

B noto‘g‘ri: mushuk kimgadir hujum qilishi haqida gap yo‘q. C noto‘g‘ri: deyarli ko‘rinmaydigan hayvon keng tarqalgan deb aytilmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: matn mushukni eshitish emas, ko‘rish haqida; shovqinli hayvonni topish osonroq bo‘lardi.

passage: When a particle detector at a mountain laboratory recorded a faint signal that recurred every 24 hours, some team members hoped it pointed to an undiscovered particle. Physicist Nargiza Abdullayeva traced the signal to the building's cooling system, which switched on each afternoon and slightly warmed the detector's electronics. The signal, she concluded, was ______: real in the sense that the instrument registered it, but produced by the equipment rather than by anything in nature.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The final clause defines the blank: the signal was really recorded but did not reflect a genuine natural phenomenon. Choice C, “spurious” (false, not what it appears to be), fits.

Choice A is wrong because “ephemeral” (short-lived) misreads the evidence: the signal returned every day, and its duration is not the point. Choice B is wrong because “intractable” (impossible to solve) contradicts the fact that Abdullayeva explained the signal. Choice D is wrong because “ubiquitous” (found everywhere) has no support; the signal came from one building's equipment.
explanation_uz:
Oxirgi qism bo‘sh joyni izohlaydi: signal haqiqatan qayd etilgan, lekin tabiatdagi haqiqiy hodisani aks ettirmagan. C javob — “spurious” (soxta, ko‘ringanidek emas) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: “ephemeral” (qisqa muddatli) dalilni noto‘g‘ri talqin qiladi — signal har kuni qaytgan, uning davomiyligi asosiy masala emas. B noto‘g‘ri: “intractable” (hal qilib bo‘lmaydigan) Abdullayeva signalni tushuntirib bergani bilan zid. D noto‘g‘ri: “ubiquitous” (hamma joyda uchraydigan) asossiz; signal bitta binoning uskunasidan chiqqan.

passage: Gallium is a soft, silvery metal with an unusually low melting point of about 30°C (86°F). Because this temperature is lower than that of the human body, a small piece of solid gallium held in a person's palm will gradually ______.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The palm is warmer than gallium's melting point, so the metal will melt. Choice A, “liquefy” (become liquid), fits.

Choice B is wrong because heat above the melting point softens a solid; it does not harden it. Choice C is wrong because melting has nothing to do with breaking into pieces. Choice D is wrong because evaporating means turning into a gas, which requires reaching a boiling point, not a melting point.
explanation_uz:
Kaft galliyning erish haroratidan issiqroq, shuning uchun metall eriydi. A javob — “liquefy” (suyuqlikka aylanmoq) to‘g‘ri.

B noto‘g‘ri: erish haroratidan yuqori issiqlik qattiq jismni yumshatadi, qotirmaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: erish bo‘laklarga sinish bilan bog‘liq emas. D noto‘g‘ri: bug‘lanish gazga aylanish demakdir, buning uchun erish emas, qaynash harorati kerak.

passage: Architect Saodat Murodova designed the village school in 1964 to be ______. Its inner walls slid along tracks in the floor, so that teachers could combine two classrooms into a hall for assemblies or divide one into small rooms for reading groups.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The sliding walls let teachers change the rooms for different needs. Choice B, “adaptable” (able to be changed for new uses), fits.

Choice A is wrong because the text describes how the building works, not decoration. Choice C is wrong because walls that move are the opposite of fixed or permanent. Choice D is wrong because nothing is said about the school's location.
explanation_uz:
Suriladigan devorlar o‘qituvchilarga xonalarni turli ehtiyojlarga moslab o‘zgartirish imkonini bergan. B javob — “adaptable” (moslashuvchan) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: matn bezaklar haqida emas, binoning qanday ishlashi haqida. C noto‘g‘ri: harakatlanadigan devorlar o‘zgarmas bo‘lishning teskarisi. D noto‘g‘ri: maktab joylashuvi haqida hech narsa aytilmagan.

passage: Market researcher Dilfuza Karimova asked shoppers in twelve cities whether they preferred paper or cloth bags. The results were remarkably ______: in every city, and in every age and income group, roughly seven out of ten people chose cloth.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The colon introduces the clue: the same result (about seven in ten choosing cloth) appeared in every city and every group. Choice C, “consistent” (the same throughout), fits.

Choice A is wrong because the text never says what anyone expected, so there is no basis for calling the results surprising. Choice B is wrong because the results are described as clear and uniform, not confusing. Choice D is wrong because the survey covered every city and group mentioned; nothing is missing.
explanation_uz:
Ikki nuqtadan keyin ishora beriladi: har bir shaharda va har bir guruhda bir xil natija (taxminan o‘ndan yetti kishi matoni tanlagan) chiqqan. C javob — “consistent” (barqaror, bir xil) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: matnda hech kim nima kutgani aytilmagan, shuning uchun natijalarni kutilmagan deyishga asos yo‘q. B noto‘g‘ri: natijalar aniq va bir xil, chalkash emas. D noto‘g‘ri: so‘rov tilga olingan barcha shahar va guruhlarni qamragan, hech narsa yetishmaydi.

passage: The trade agreement signed by the river cities of Duraband and Kesh in 1872 was meant to cover only a single harvest season, and merchants on both sides expected it to lapse once the cotton crop had been sold. Instead, it was renewed so routinely for the next sixty years that later traders assumed it had always existed. What its authors had conceived as a ______ arrangement became one of the most enduring features of regional commerce.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The agreement was “meant to cover only a single harvest season” and expected to lapse, and the sentence contrasts that plan with how “enduring” it became. Choice A, “provisional” (temporary, intended only for the present), fits.

Choice B is wrong because “clandestine” (secret) has no support; merchants on both sides knew of the agreement. Choice C is wrong because the text never discusses whether the deal was profitable. Choice D is wrong because, although an agreement between two cities may be “reciprocal” (mutual), that word does not create the contrast with “enduring” that the sentence requires.
explanation_uz:
Kelishuv “faqat bitta hosil mavsumi uchun” mo‘ljallangan va muddati tugaydi deb kutilgan; gap bu rejani uning qanchalik “uzoq umrli” bo‘lib chiqqani bilan qarama-qarshi qo‘yadi. A javob — “provisional” (vaqtinchalik) to‘g‘ri.

B noto‘g‘ri: “clandestine” (yashirin) asossiz — ikki tomon savdogarlari kelishuvni bilgan. C noto‘g‘ri: kelishuv foydali bo‘lgani muhokama qilinmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: ikki shahar o‘rtasidagi kelishuv “reciprocal” (o‘zaro) bo‘lishi mumkin, ammo bu so‘z gap talab qiladigan “uzoq umrli” bilan qarama-qarshilikni yaratmaydi.

passage: In 1925 the directors of the Oydin Silk Company ______ a proposal to build a second warehouse. Rather than approve or reject the plan, they asked its supporters for revised cost estimates and agreed to vote on it again the following spring.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The directors neither approved nor rejected the plan; they postponed the decision until spring. Choice D, “tabled” (set aside for later discussion), fits.

Choice A is wrong because the text says they did not approve it. Choice B is wrong because they did not reject it either; they planned to vote again. Choice C is wrong because asking for revised estimates shows caution, not celebration.
explanation_uz:
Direktorlar rejani na ma’qulladi, na rad etdi; ular qarorni bahorgacha qoldirdi. D javob — “tabled” (keyinga qoldirildi) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: matnga ko‘ra ular rejani ma’qullamagan. B noto‘g‘ri: rad ham etmagan, yana ovoz berishni rejalashtirgan. C noto‘g‘ri: qayta hisob-kitob so‘rash bayram emas, ehtiyotkorlikni ko‘rsatadi.

passage: The city's new recycling rules were published only in a forty-page technical document full of legal terms. Not surprisingly, many residents found the rules ______: a survey found that fewer than a third of households could say which items belonged in which bin.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The rules were buried in a long, technical document, and most households could not say which items went in which bin. Choice A, “confusing” (hard to understand), fits.

Choice B is wrong because nothing suggests the rules give residents extra benefits. Choice C is wrong because the survey measured understanding, not approval. Choice D is wrong because the rules are described as new.
explanation_uz:
Qoidalar uzun texnik hujjatda berilgan va ko‘pchilik oilalar qaysi narsa qaysi qutiga tushishini ayta olmagan. A javob — “confusing” (chalkash, tushunish qiyin) to‘g‘ri.

B noto‘g‘ri: qoidalar aholiga qo‘shimcha imtiyoz bergani haqida gap yo‘q. C noto‘g‘ri: so‘rov qoidalar ma’qullanishini emas, tushunilishini o‘lchagan. D noto‘g‘ri: qoidalar yangi deb ta’riflangan.

passage:
The following text is from a short story.

As the train pulled away from the station, Laylo pressed her forehead against the window. She had waited eight months for this journey, and now that it had finally begun, she was too ______ to sit still: she checked her ticket again, retied her scarf twice, and grinned at nothing in particular.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
Laylo has long waited for the trip, cannot sit still, and grins. Choice D, “excited” (eager and full of energy), fits.

Choice A is wrong because a tired person would not fidget and grin. Choice B is wrong because she clearly cares a great deal about the journey. Choice C is wrong because grinning shows happiness, not sadness.
explanation_uz:
Laylo bu safarni uzoq kutgan, joyida o‘tira olmaydi va jilmayadi. D javob — “excited” (hayajonlangan) to‘g‘ri.

A noto‘g‘ri: charchagan odam bezovtalanib, jilmayib o‘tirmaydi. B noto‘g‘ri: u safarga juda katta ahamiyat beradi. C noto‘g‘ri: jilmayish qayg‘uni emas, quvonchni ko‘rsatadi.

passage: Ecologist Rano Ibragimova first blamed pollution for the sharp decline in the number of frogs in Lake Sarvi. But repeated water tests found no harmful chemicals, and many of the dead frogs showed signs of a fungal infection. These findings led Ibragimova to ______ her original explanation and focus on disease instead.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The tests contradicted the pollution idea, and Ibragimova turned her attention to disease “instead.” Choice A, “abandon” (give up), fits.

Choice B is wrong because the evidence went against her original explanation. Choice C is wrong because publishing an explanation the evidence had undermined would not lead her to focus on disease “instead.” Choice D is wrong because she replaced the explanation rather than expanding it.
explanation_uz:
Sinovlar ifloslanish haqidagi fikrni rad etgan va Ibragimova e’tiborini uning “o‘rniga” kasallikka qaratgan. A javob — “abandon” (voz kechmoq) to‘g‘ri.

B noto‘g‘ri: dalillar uning dastlabki tushuntirishiga zid. C noto‘g‘ri: dalillar zaiflashtirgan tushuntirishni nashr qilish uni kasallikka “o‘rniga” e’tibor berishga olib kelmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: u tushuntirishni kengaytirmagan, almashtirgan.

passage: Some geologists have argued that the steep, narrow shape of the Qorasuv Canyon could only have been carved by a single catastrophic flood. Geologist Komil Abdurahmonov disagrees. His analysis of the canyon walls reveals thousands of thin sediment layers, each laid down by an ordinary seasonal stream, one year after another. The canyon, he concludes, is the product not of one dramatic event but of ______ processes.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
Abdurahmonov rejects the single-flood idea and points to thousands of thin layers laid down “one year after another.” Choice B, “incremental” (happening in small steps over time), fits the contrast with “one dramatic event.”

Choice A is wrong because “cataclysmic” (violently destructive) describes the flood theory he rejects. Choice C is wrong because “sporadic” (occurring irregularly) conflicts with layers deposited regularly each season. Choice D is wrong because “tectonic” (relating to movements of Earth's crust) is not supported; the evidence concerns sediment from streams.
explanation_uz:
Abdurahmonov bitta toshqin g‘oyasini rad etadi va “yildan-yilga” hosil bo‘lgan minglab yupqa qatlamlarga ishora qiladi. B javob — “incremental” (asta-sekin, kichik qadamlar bilan) “bitta keskin hodisa”ga qarama-qarshilikka mos keladi.

A noto‘g‘ri: “cataclysmic” (halokatli) u rad etgan toshqin nazariyasini tasvirlaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: “sporadic” (tartibsiz, vaqti-vaqti bilan) har mavsumda muntazam to‘plangan qatlamlarga zid. D noto‘g‘ri: “tectonic” (yer po‘stining harakatiga oid) asossiz; dalillar oqimlar keltirgan cho‘kindilar haqida.

passage: Early computer models predicted that a new antibiotic would be broken down by the liver within a few hours. Blood tests by pharmacologist Aziza Qodirova told a different story: the drug ______ in patients' bloodstreams for nearly two days, which means doses may need to be spaced much further apart.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The models predicted the drug would be gone within hours, but the tests showed otherwise, and doses may need to be spaced further apart. So the drug remained in the blood much longer. Choice A, “persisted” (continued to exist), fits.

Choice B is wrong because “dissolved” suggests disappearing, which matches the prediction the text rejects. Choice C is wrong because the drug was given to patients; it did not originate in their blood. Choice D is wrong because the text is about how long the drug lasted, not about anything speeding up.
explanation_uz:
Modellar dori bir necha soatda yo‘qoladi deb taxmin qilgan, ammo sinovlar boshqacha natija bergan va dozalar orasini uzaytirish kerak bo‘lishi mumkin. Demak, dori qonda ancha uzoq qolgan. A javob — “persisted” (saqlanib qoldi) to‘g‘ri.

B noto‘g‘ri: “dissolved” (erib ketdi) yo‘qolishni bildiradi, bu esa matn rad etgan taxminga mos. C noto‘g‘ri: dori bemorlarga berilgan, u qonda paydo bo‘lmagan. D noto‘g‘ri: matn biror narsa tezlashgani haqida emas, dorining qancha saqlangani haqida.

passage: The early poems of the poet Sabohat Nuriddinova were notably ______, packed with allusions to little-known legends and rare words that few readers could follow without a dictionary at hand. Her later poems, by contrast, use the plain language of everyday conversation.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The early poems are full of little-known legends and rare words that few readers could follow, and they are contrasted with later poems in plain language. Choice A, “esoteric” (understood by only a few people with special knowledge), fits.

Choice B is wrong because “colloquial” (like everyday speech) describes the later poems, not the early ones. Choice C is wrong because nothing suggests the poems were funny. Choice D is wrong because being “packed with” allusions concerns difficulty, not brevity.
explanation_uz:
Ilk she’rlar kam ma’lum afsonalar va kamdan-kam so‘zlarga to‘la bo‘lib, ularni ozchilik o‘quvchi tushuna olgan; ular oddiy tildagi keyingi she’rlarga qarama-qarshi qo‘yilgan. A javob — “esoteric” (faqat tor doiraga tushunarli) to‘g‘ri.

B noto‘g‘ri: “colloquial” (so‘zlashuv tiliga xos) keyingi she’rlarni tasvirlaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: she’rlar kulgili bo‘lgani aytilmagan. D noto‘g‘ri: ishoralarga “to‘la” bo‘lish qisqalik emas, murakkablik haqida.
